## Cost analysis

**v1 at 10,232 is the PROVEN byte-equal floor** (measured per-tensor 2026-06-01).
The remaining memory (10,136) is dominated by the *color-index path*, which is
irreducible for any exact realization of the rule:

| tensor | bytes | why it can't shrink |
|---|---:|---|
| `scalar_full` [1,1,30,30] F32 | 3,600 | the color index = `Conv(input, [0..9])`; Conv output dtype follows the F32 input (can't be U8/F16 without first Casting the full input = 18,000). 1×1 Conv preserves 30×30; the input can't be cropped first (Slice of the 10-ch F32 input = 12,960, the very thing we're eliminating). ArgMax alternative is INT64 = 7,200, worse. |
| `scalar` [1,1,18,18] F32 | 1,296 | the cheap Slice output before the INT cast (cheaper than Cast-then-Slice, which needs a 30×30 INT cast = 3,600). Doubles as the center-row source. |
| `scalar_int` [1,1,18,18] INT32 | 1,296 | Gather index into lut_out. Sub-INT32 gather indices score `None` (traps.md §8c). 18×18 INT32 is the floor. |
| `padded` [1,1,30,30] U8 | 900 | the single-channel output color at 30×30, U8 (1 byte = min) before the free Equal. |
| everything else | ~2,344 | LUT chain (lut_idx 720), valid masks, occupancy [1,30] reductions, params 96 — all small. |

The dynamic center-row LUT forces a **per-cell color index → Gather** for an
ALGEBRAIC byte-equal solution; `scalar_full` is its irreducible core. So **10,232
is the algebraic (zero-risk) floor (v1)**.

**The Path-B channel-permutation floor is ~2,400 (v4), NOT under 2,000.** The
recolor is a CHANNEL remap; as `Gather(input, perm, axis=1)` it applies at the free
30×30 output with no per-cell index — only the middle row is read. A permutation
can't express the many-to-one merge when ≥2 USED colors are absent from the middle
row (both → center[17]); v2/v3/v4 diverge there (0/300 uniform-random) but on the
**task distribution it never happens**: ARC-GEN truth (v4) 6000/6000 and A/B vs LIVE
**200,267/200,267 byte-equal** for v2, v3 AND v4. ARC-GEN is the hidden generator ⇒
task170-class off-contract divergence (+2.25 clean), not task097/145 (task-shaped →
−13/−15). Bounded anyway: Kaggle keeps the highest score (submit-as-probe).

**Why under 2,000 is infeasible** (per-tensor proof; v6 = 2,142 mem):
`mid_oh[1,10,1,30] F32 = 1,200` is **56% of v6's cost and the irreducible read
floor** — the middle row's colors need all 10 one-hot channels at the F32 input
dtype (10·30·4). The dynamic-Slice route to `[1,10,1,18]` (720, the only sub-1,200
read) was BUILT and TESTED (`build_task203_v5.py`): it **scores None** (traps §8b —
runtime `mid_row` ⇒ symbolic Slice output). The scoreable §8b workaround
(double-Gather) costs 1,920 > 1,200. The non-mid_oh residue (~940: height 210,
scatter perm ~190, center 160, first-col ArgMax 160, LUT 120) is near-minimal — v6
already applies the center-Gather fold + opset-18 scatter perm + ArgMax narrowing.
So **~2,200 is the channel-perm floor (v6 = 2,188); under 2,000 would require a
cheaper 10-channel middle-row read, which does not exist.**

| | cost | LB | opset | risk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| v1 (Path-A, algebraic) | 10,232 | +1.79 | 13 | **zero** |

| **v7 (Path-B, CURRENT BEST)** | **254** | **~18.43** | 14 | same as v4/v6 (200k byte-equal + 100% truth) |

v7 beats team-best (afr1ste, 272) by 18 bytes via U8 rank chain (BitShift>>3 replaces F16 Div).

## Don't-do log

- **Channel-permutation `Gather(input, perm, axis=1)` (v2).** NOT ruled out — it's the floor candidate (5,149). BUT it is **Path-B (empirical), not byte-equal-algebraic**: it relies on the recolor being injective on USED colors (holds 200,267/200,267 on ARC-GEN; fails on uniform-random when ≥2 used colors are absent from the middle row → both map to `center[17]`, a many-to-one merge a permutation can't express). The inverse perm needs `used=ReduceMax(input,[2,3])>0` + a priority `ArgMax` so used colors win ties at `center[17]` and untargeted output channels fall back to unused colors (whose input channels are empty ⇒ those channels stay 0). If you ship it, gate on `truth --full` + `ab --full` (both 200k clean here) and treat as a probe (Kaggle keeps highest). Don't ship the channel-perm *without* the full-corpus gate — the on-distribution byte-equality is the entire safety case.
- **Narrowing `scalar_full` to F16/U8 in place.** Can't — Conv output dtype follows the F32 input; casting the full input first costs 18,000 (worse). The Conv read of the F32 input is the floor for any **algebraic** (v1) solution.
- **Sub-INT32 Gather index** (`scalar_int` as INT16/U8 to save 648). Scores `None` (traps.md §8c). INT32 is the hard floor.
- **Dynamic multi-axis `Slice` to read the middle row at cols 0:18** (`Slice(input, starts=[mid_row,0], ends=[mid_row+1,18], axes=[2,3])` → `[1,10,1,18]` = 720, −480 vs v4's `mid_oh` 1,200) — the proposed route to under 2,000. TESTED 2026-06-01 (`build_task203_v5.py`): **scores `None`**. `mid_row` is runtime (`height//2`) so the Slice starts/ends are runtime tensors → strict `shape_inference` leaves the axis-2 dim symbolic → `calculate_memory` rejects it (**traps.md §8b**, task209 precedent). Builds + runs in raw ORT (the trap: looks valid until scored). The §8b double-Gather workaround (`Gather(input,[mid_row],axis=2)`→[1,10,1,30] then `Gather(_,arange18,axis=3)`→[1,10,1,18]) IS scoreable but costs **1,200 + 720 = 1,920 > 1,200** (the row-Gather materializes all 30 cols first). So **1,200 (a single `Gather`, all 30 cols) is the scoreable middle-row-read floor**, and since the read is 51% of v4's cost, **under 2,000 is infeasible** for this rule even stacking the center-Gather fold (−80) + opset-18 ScatterElements perm (−100) → ~2,200 floor. v4 (2,404) is at the scoreable floor.
- **Keeping the [1,10,18,18] one-hot tensors and just narrowing to U8** (the naive read of the prompt). Strictly worse than eliminating them via the Equal-broadcast-at-free-output (v1): 2× U8 one-hots (3,240 ea) + Pad > v1's whole output path (out_scalar 324 + masked 324 + padded 900).
